description: Single and two storey side to rear extension;  Single storey side extension; Roof lights in rear roof slope; External alterations (Demolition of rear extension, double garage, conservatory, side canopy, oil store and removal of swimming pool)
decision_conditions: The proposed extensions, by reason of their excessive bulk, scale, and massing, would cause harm to the special architectural and historic interest of the locally listed Pinnerwood Cottage, fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Pinnerwood Farm Conservation Area, and would adversely affect the setting of both the locally listed Pinnerwood Farmhouse and the Grade II listed Pinnerwood House. No clear and convincing justification has been provided for this harm, nor are there any public benefits which would outweigh it and the proposal is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CS1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012); Policies DM1 and DM7 of Harrow’s Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), the Harrow Residential Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010), and the Pinnerwood Farm Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Strategy (2009).

The proposed development, by reason of its design, excessive bulk, height, massing and consolidated form, would constitute a disproportionate addition over and above the original dwellinghouse and therefore represents inappropriate development in the Green Belt, resulting in harm to its openness and rural character. No ‘very special circumstances’ have been demonstrated to clearly outweigh this harm and the proposal is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CS1.B and CS1.F of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), and Policies DM1 and DM16 of Harrow’s Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).
